notes:
Account summary: AegisHelm is a mid-market CCaaS vendor that bundles omnichannel routing + bot orchestration. Evaluating Redwood for agent-assist RAG over multi-source KBs (Zendesk, Confluence, SQL dumps, S3), ticket summarization, and triggering tool-calls (ticket updates, SLA escalations) from the assistant. Strong emphasis on citations + freshness and predictable behavior during traffic spikes.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-28: Intro call (Jordan Lee) — discussed Redwood product tiers; AE demo showed streaming + function-calling.
- 2026-02-12: Tech deep-dive with infra & data eng (Priya present) — walked architecture; customer runs Elastic + Confluence + legacy DB, wants unified retriever. Action: share retrieval patterns doc.
- 2026-02-25: Legal & Security pre-screen — asked for SOC2/ISO evidence, KMS details, data residency options. Uploaded SOC2 summary to Drive.
- 2026-03-01: Kickoff POC call (ff-20260301-aegishelm-call-7x9k) — agreed on 3-week POC: 1) ingest sample KB, 2) implement citation-enabled RAG pipeline, 3) validate 95th pctl latency for agent assist and function-calls.

Technical requirements / POC acceptance criteria:
- RAG: must return top-3 citations with provenance (source, last-modified) and highlight excerpt. Need hybrid retrieval: BM25 over docs + vector search for semantic match.
- Freshness: docs updated hourly; ingest incremental updates and surface "stale" flag if source older than 24h.
- Throughput & latency: interactive agent-assist target end-to-end 200-350ms for cached hits, cold RAG allowed up to 800ms. During incident spikes expect up to 6k rps for short windows — need graceful degradation and fallback to smaller model or precomputed summaries.
- Tool-calling: assistant must be able to POST to their ticketing API (auth via mTLS/token) and confirm idempotency; audit entries required for every automated ticket update.
- Summaries: nightly batch summarization of backlog tickets with changelog linking (must be re-runnable).
- Security: SSO/SAML for console, per-route audit logs, customer-managed KMS, data residency in us-east-1 for EU customers not allowed.

Architecture preferences discussed:
- Prefers private deployment inside their VPC for compliance; open to Redwood Dedicated if private full on-prem isn't necessary. Wants dedicated GPU pool for predictable p50/p95.
- Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions: quantization recommendations for their retrieval-heavy queries and batching recommendations for throughput bursts.
- Wants automatic prefix/KV caching for commonly-referenced KBs (how caching interacts with citation freshness unclear).

POC plan & milestones:
- Week 0: sample data ingest (Zendesk export, Confluence pages, DB dump) + baseline metrics (latency/cost/token usage).
- Week 1: implement RAG pipeline with citation metadata + simple reranker; compare vector store options (FAISS vs managed).
- Week 2: instrument tool-calls + end-to-end agent-assist scenario; run spike tests (5000-6000 rps for 2 min bursts).
- Week 3: security checklist, SOC2 artifact review, handoff to procurement.

Quotes / stakeholder notes:
- Head of Product: "Citations are non-negotiable — agents need source links in every answer."
- Platform lead: "We will not accept a black-box retriever; need inspectable retrieval logs & TTL controls."

Open questions / risks:

- Cost model for sustained vs burst capacity: customer wants hybrid reserved + burst.
- Legal: can Redwood commit to data residency SLA in contract?

- Jordan to deliver POC latency/cost profile and recommended deployment (private vs dedicated) by 2026-03-15.
